title: Lean No-Sorry Account v0

canonical_node.axiom: The public claim about Lean proof strength must be based on verified no-sorry builds and proof-strength classification, not raw declaration counts.
definitions: no-sorry source text: a Lean file with no active sorry or admit proof holes
proof-strength class: a category such as SUBSTANTIVE_OR_CASE_PROOF, FINITE_DECIDABLE, SIMPLIFICATION, DEFINITIONAL_RFL, TRIVIAL_TRUE, WRAPPER_OR_IMPORTED, DECLARATION_OR_UNKNOWN
raw theorem/lemma declaration: any theorem or lemma statement in a Lean file, regardless of proof strength
derivation: The workspace contains 91 Lean file copies, deduplicated to 44 unique source texts by SHA256.
Of these, 43 are likely unique no-sorry source texts; 1 is a sorry-bearing spec file.
Across the unique Lean texts, there are about 880 raw theorem/lemma declarations.
The proof-strength summary shows only 43 substantive or case proofs, with many definitional, trivial, or wrapper declarations.
Therefore, the raw count of 880 must not be presented as deep proofs.
A no-sorry text scan is not equivalent to a clean build; further verification is required.
canonical_node.action: Report the no-sorry inventory as 'about 43 unique no-sorry Lean source texts' and 'about 880 raw theorem/lemma declarations' only with the caveat that proof-strength classification is pending. Do not claim machine-checked proof counts until a clean build and classification are completed.
boundary: Does not assert that any Lean file has been successfully compiled or verified.
Does not equate raw declaration counts with proof strength.
Does not claim that the 43 no-sorry files are all substantive proofs.
Does not provide a final machine-checked proof count.
test: Check that any public statement about Lean proofs includes the qualifier 'no-sorry candidate inventory' unless a clean build log exists.
Verify that the proof-strength summary is used instead of raw theorem counts when describing substantive proofs.
Confirm that the single sorry-bearing spec file is not counted as a no-sorry source.

dg1_dependencies: Lean source files in the workspace
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a conservative inventory of no-sorry Lean source texts and raw declaration counts, with explicit caution against overclaiming proof strength.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the distinction between raw declarations and verified proofs, preventing inflation of the proof count.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this node, the raw 880 declaration count could be misreported as 880 deep proofs, misleading stakeholders.

classification.recommended_atom_action: Use as a conservative inventory; do not upgrade to verified proof count without further build verification.

overstatement_risks: Interpreting raw declaration counts as deep proofs
Assuming no-sorry text scan implies successful compilation
Ignoring proof-strength classification when reporting substantive proofs
kill_conditions: If a clean build of the no-sorry package fails, the inventory is invalid.
If the proof-strength summary is found to be inaccurate, the classification is invalid.
risk.lean_target: A verified Lean build log with per-theorem proof-strength classification.

plain_summary: This document provides a conservative count of no-sorry Lean files and raw theorem declarations, warning that these numbers are not proof counts. It emphasizes the need for further verification and classification before making stronger claims.
